objectives: The objective of this course is to develop students’ ability to read, analyze, and assess written texts in academic and professional contexts. We will explore the importance of reading in a wide range of activities, including independent critical thinking and social and political participation. The course is designed to equip students with the necessary reading skills for more advanced courses and their professional lives after college.
content: Class activities will consist of short in-class readings, brief writing responses, and group work on questions related to the readings.  Along with the in-class readings, students will be given study questions with analytical frameworks for thinking critically about each text. These handouts will also introduce new vocabulary and relevant historical and cultural background. Following each reading, class meetings will consist of independent writing responses or student-led discussions in pairs, groups, and as a class. The midterm and final exams will be in-class essays (closed book; no electronic devices; a print dictionary will be provided).
grading_policy: All conversation in this course will be conducted in English. Grades will be calculated according to students’ weekly participation (40%), a midterm exam (15%), and a final exam (25%). Attendance is mandatory: two unexcused absences are permitted; a third will result in a conference with the instructor. More than three absences are grounds for failing the class. Students must also come to class on time.
